body.statement: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be compact convex subsets of linear topological spaces.  If a real function on \(M\times N\) is upper semicontinuous and quasi-concave in its first argument and lower semicontinuous and quasi-convex in its second argument, then its max--min equals its min--max.  In particular, the equality applies to a continuous function that is affine in one argument and convex in the other, after interchanging signs and arguments as needed.

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be convex, compact spaces, and \(f\) a function on \(M\times N\), quasi-concave-convex and u.s.c.-l.s.c. Then \(\sup\inf f=\inf\sup f\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Maurice Sion, On general minimax theorems, Pacific Journal of Mathematics 8 (1958), Theorem 3.4, publisher PDF.
